title: Serialize validated rows to RFC-style CSV text
prompt: Implement formatCell and escapeCell in src/cell.js and serializeCsv in src/csv.js, then re-export all three functions from src/index.js. Use ES modules and only Node built-ins. formatCell(value) returns '' for null or undefined, the unchanged string for strings, 'true' or 'false' for booleans, and String(value) for finite numbers. It throws a TypeError for NaN, Infinity, bigint, symbol, function, array, or any other object. escapeCell(value) calls formatCell and, if the resulting text contains a comma, double quote, carriage return, or newline, returns the text wrapped in double quotes with every double quote doubled; otherwise it returns the text unchanged. serializeCsv(headers, rows) requires headers to be a non-empty array of unique non-empty strings; duplicates are compared case-sensitively. rows must be an array, and every row must be an array with exactly headers.length fields. The result must contain one header line followed by one line per row, joined with '\n' with no trailing newline. Apply the same escaping rules to headers and data fields, use a comma as the only delimiter, and do not mutate either argument. An empty rows array returns only the escaped header line. Throw an Error for invalid headers, non-array rows, a row with the wrong width, or an unsupported field value.
